system:
You extract quantitative facts about one clinical trial programme from one document.

Rules:
- Extract only facts stated in THIS document. Never use outside knowledge.
- Every fact needs "quote": an exact, verbatim span copied from the document (8-300 characters) that contains the number. Quotes are machine-checked; paraphrases are discarded.
- Placebo-adjusted values are preferred. If a value is within-arm (not placebo-adjusted), set attrs.placebo_adjusted=false.
- Units: keep the unit the document uses; put it in "unit".
- Other trials of the same investigational drug (phase 2, dose-finding, other populations, combination arms) belong
  to the programme: extract their facts too, and put the trial's name in attrs.trial when the document gives it.
- Return {"facts": []} only if the document reports no results for the investigational drug.

Allowed keys:
  n_randomized, median_followup, primary_endpoint, inclusion_threshold, planned_events, assumed_rrr, power,
  alpha, stopped_early, events_treatment, events_control, events_total, hr, ci_low, ci_high, p_value,
  biomarker_change, baseline_level, sbp_change, safety_signal, readout_statement

For biomarker_change and baseline_level, attrs must include: biomarker (one of LDL-C, non-HDL-C, apoB, HDL-C,
Lp(a), triglycerides, hsCRP, IL-6, Lp-PLA2 activity, sPLA2-IIA, SBP, other), phase (phase2 or phase3),
timepoint, method (assay or "not stated"), placebo_adjusted (true/false), dose (if stated).
For biomarker_change give "value" as the change (negative = reduction) and state in attrs.kind whether it is
"percent" or "absolute".

Return JSON only:
{"facts": [{"key": "...", "value": <number or string>, "unit": "...", "attrs": {...}, "quote": "..."}]}

Investigational drug: atorvastatin
Document: Treatment with atorvastatin alters the ratio of interleukin-12/interleukin-10 gene expression [corrected] (journal, published 2003-01-01, source pmid:12492458)

--- DOCUMENT TEXT ---
Treatment with atorvastatin alters the ratio of interleukin-12/interleukin-10 gene expression [corrected]

BACKGROUND: Statins have been shown to have pleiotropic effects extending beyond their ability to lower cholesterol. MATERIAL AND METHODS: Seventeen patients with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia participated in a single-blind placebo controlled study. The patients underwent three treatment regimens: placebo (4 weeks), atorvastatin 10 mg day(-1) (4 weeks) and atorvastatin 40 mg day(-1) (12 weeks). Following each treatment period, serum lipids and plasma mevalonic acid were measured, mononuclear leukocytes were isolated and total RNA was prepared. The content of mRNA for IL-12p35 and IL-10 was assayed, blinded, by real-time quantitative polymerase chain reactions. RESULTS: Treatment of the subjects with atorvastatin decreased the abundance of IL-12p35 mRNA in mononuclear cells, but did not alter that of IL-10, so that the ratio of the IL-12p35 to IL-10 mRNA content was significantly reduced (P < 0.0026). The IL-12p35/IL-10 ratio correlated significantly with plasma mevalonic acid concentrations but not with serum LDL concentrations. CONCLUSIONS: This study provides evidence that atorvastatin exerts an immunomodulatory effect in vivo, characterized by a decrease in the ratio of IL-12 mRNA to IL-10 mRNA in leukocytes. The immunomodulatory effect of statins, in addition to their cholesterol-lowering properties, may contribute to the rapid cardiovascular benefit observed during treatment with statins and reduced the rate of rejection in patients with solid organ transplantation.
--- END ---
